audit_items.proof_trace: The sum invariant (referrer_bps + referee_bps < 10000) is not enforced: update_referral_params validates each bps individually against DENOMINATOR (L250-251) but never checks their combined sum, allowing e.g. referrer=9000 + referee=9000=18000 to pass. The sequential computation in track_flash_loan_usage (L132-138) prevents arithmetic overflow (referrer receives a fraction of the fee remaining after referee's share, so total rebates always < initial_fee), but the stored invariant is violated and the protocol could be configured to retain near-zero flash loan fees.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An AdminCap holder (or compromised admin key) calls update_referral_params with referrer_discount_bps=9000 and referee_discount_bps=9000; subsequently every flash loan distributes ~99% of its fee as rebates (90% to referee, then 90% of remaining to referrer), leaving the protocol with ~1% of fee revenue.
